newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says it concerned for Sudanese people.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says it concerned for Sudanese people.

text.p: A senior Egyptian official said on Sunday it was out of concern for the Sudanese people that Egypt supported a Security Council decision to delay for a month any moves towards implementing an air embargo on Sudan.

Sayyed Kassem, assistant foreign minister for multilateral affairs, told reporters Egypt also wanted to give Sudan more time to reconsider its position and to hand over three men wanted for an attempt to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"A principal element in Egypt's position is to prevent an increase in the suffering of the Sudanese people," Kassem said.
"The aim of these sanctions is to put pressure on the ruling Sudanese regime to make them respond to the requests of the international community and not to punish the Sudanese people," he added.
The council decided in mid-August to impose the air ban but postponed setting a starting date for at least 90 days.
France called for a 30-day delay in deciding on a date for the air embargo to allow time for a report on the humanitarian impact of the new measures. This was supported by Russia and Egypt.
Sudan says an air embargo would have dire humanitarian effects, such as preventing imports of medicines and travel by thousands of Sudanese seeking medical treatment abroad.
Sudan is already the target of mandatory diplomatic and travel sanctions that went into effect on May 10 after a two-week grace period.
A Sudanese official said on Saturday his country hoped the delay would give the United Nations time to reconsider the move.

Sudan continued to maintain it had no trace of the three men wanted for involvement in a plot to assassinate Mubarak after he arrived in Addis Ababa on June 26, 1995, for a summit of the Organisation of African Unity.
The Sudanese government says it has complied with Security Council resolutions and provided all information available but says Egypt and Ethiopia have not cooperated.

The air embargo decided in principle in August would require all countries to deny permission to aircraft registered in Sudan, or leased or operated by Sudan Airways or the Sudanese government, to take off from, land in or overfly their territory.
